$comment: Who may read and write each model of prisma/schema/time.prisma (rules: src/ownership.ts; roles: src/roles.ts). Time and attendance is personal data with one purpose, ATTENDANCE (GDPR art. 5(1)(b); Statuto dei Lavoratori art. 4 c.2): every row of a personal table is about one person: its `personal` entry names the subject (employeeId) and tags each personal column with the purpose ATTENDANCE (the privacy export and erasure read them, and the floor reads only ATTENDANCE-tagged columns); OvertimeRequest, AbsenceCode, AttendanceMonthClose and WorkingTimeRule name no person. The office (apps/factory-api's People steps B-W2b-32, -33, -37, -42, -48: HR, and the leads for their own team, through the API's permissions and the legal gate of B-W2b-27) reads and writes, always through command(). The floor of a site (factory_floor_runtime, scoped by its site) records its clock events and reads them (the worker's own time today, the offline queue's repeats), reads its PUBLISHED roster rows and the overtime it is asked, records a worker's own answer to an ask (FLOOR only; the …_time_w2b_guards triggers refuse any other change from the floor), and reads which months are closed (the clock-event trigger refuses an event dated in a closed month), never a month's file or who closed it. Attendance days, anomalies, absences, overtime entries, timesheets, corrections, absence codes and working-time limits are the office's only. Portal and link sessions (factory_partner_runtime) and the platform role read nothing here. ClockEvent and AttendanceCorrection are append-only (`@append-only`; the triggers refuse UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE for every login): no role updates or deletes them. Nothing else is deleted but a roster cell, a person taken off an ask, an absence and an overtime entry being recomputed, while their month is open (and an OPEN month close abandoned). After a change run `npm run policies -w @nexus/factory-db -- <folder>`.

RosterEntry.about: The office sets one person's shift (or day off) per day on the roster sheet, copies a week, publishes it and takes a cell back to the default; nothing changes in a closed month. The floor of the site reads its PUBLISHED rows only (a worker's own shifts, the next break).

OvertimeRequest.about: The office plans overtime for a date and line, asks people, approves it, marks it done or cancels it with a reason; never deleted. The floor of the site reads the asks from ASKED on (not a draft), never who asked, approved or why it was cancelled.

OvertimeAgreement.about: The office adds the people asked (and takes a pending one off) and records an answer told to the lead or HR. The floor of the site reads its asks and records the worker's own answer on its tablet (FLOOR, with the worker and the device); the trigger refuses any other change from the floor.

ClockEvent.about: The floor of a site records clock-ins, clock-outs and breaks (badge, name and PIN, offline) and reads its site's events (the worker's own time today; the offline queue's repeats are refused by the tablet's event id). The office records MANUAL events with a reason, the automatic clock-out (AUTO) and a VOID of a mistaken event, and reads every event. Nobody changes or removes one.

AttendanceDay.about: The office computes one person's day from the clock events and the roster, marks it to fix, approves it, reopens it, and closes it at the month close; never deleted. The floor reads none (a worker's own day reaches My day through the API, behind the PIN and the legal gate).

AttendanceAnomaly.about: The office raises what is wrong with a day (the rule that found it) and resolves it once (fixed, accepted with a note, or cleared by a new computation); never deleted.

AbsenceCode.about: HR keeps the tenant's and its companies' absence codes (the consultant's LUL code, paid, document needed) and archives them; never deleted.

AbsenceEntry.about: HR and the leads enter one person's absence per day and code (ahead, for a planned holiday, or after), change it and remove it while its month is open.

OvertimeEntry.about: The office records the overtime worked per person, day and class, approves or rejects it (paid only once approved) and recomputes a pending one (removed and written again) while its month is open.

TimesheetApproval.about: The lead, then HR (another person), approve one person's timesheet for a period; either sends it back with a reason. Frozen once its month is closed; never deleted.

AttendanceMonthClose.about: HR starts a company's month close, closes it once its days are closed (no anomaly open, no overtime waiting), and seals the LUL attendance calendar on it; a closed month never opens again; an OPEN one may be abandoned (deleted). The floor reads which months are closed (company, month, status), never the file, its seal, the note or who closed it.

AttendanceCorrection.about: HR corrects a closed day's figure with a new entry (from → to, with its reason) for the payroll's correction export. Nobody changes or removes one.

WorkingTimeRule.about: HR keeps the working-time limits (tenant-wide, a company's or a site's; the law's value or the CCNL's; warn or block; who is alerted) and archives them; never deleted. The planning and approval checks read them.
